sentences.text: At the outset, we make it clear that the chronology of events that have unfolded in passing the Orders under review are crucial in deciding this Review Petition.
It will not only show how the Orders of this Court have not been taken seriously by the Government officers but also how they tend to mislead the Courts in matters like this.
We are constrained to write this in the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case.
3. Relevant chronology of events for deciding this Review Petition are as under.

3.1) Some time in the year 2020 - The Original Petitioners filed a Writ Petition (St) No. 98385 of 2020 in this Court, inter alia, praying for a Writ of Mandamus to complete acquisition proceedings as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ("RTFCLARR Act"
for short) in a time bound manner and to calculate & pay the compensation and for an order and direction to determine Tikam page 2 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc and pay rental compensation to the Petitioners.

sentences.text: 3.2) 28th January, 2021 -

This Court disposed of the said Writ Petition after recording that the State Government had filed an affidavit therein, inter alia, stating that the Sub-Divisional Offier will hear the Petitioners and/or their Advocates before passing an Award, and that the said Award passed will be passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer not later than March, 2021.
This Court accepted the statements as an undertaking given to this Court.
It was clarified and directed that the SDO shall also decide the claim of the Petitioners pertaining to the rental compensation.
All the contentions of the parties were kept open.

3.3) 7th May, 2021 - Since the above order was not complied in time, the Original Petitioners, filed Contempt Petition No. 769 of 2021 (out of which present matter arises) in this Court alleging disobedience of the order passed by this Court dt. 28th January 2021.

3.4) 27th May 2021 - The concerned SDO (who happens to be the present Review Petitioner - Mr. Udaysingh Bhosale) passed an award determining the compensation amount of Rs.13,42,19,901/- payable to the Original Petitioners.
3.5) 17th January 2023 :

The said contempt petition was listed before us for the first time, when the copy of the award Tikam page 3 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc passed (dated 27th May 2021) was placed on record by Ld. senior Counsel for the original Petitioners.

It was pointed out that though in para 3 (including a chart thereunder) dealing with Owners' objections it is opined by the SDO, Magalvedha that 9% and 15% interest is payable to owners by Dist. 4. From the aforesaid statements made by the Review Petitioner in a companion matter and original Respondent No.4 (Sub- divisional Water Conservation Officer), an impression was sought to be created in our minds
that our Order disposing of the Contempt Tikam page 8 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc Petition under 1st Order dated 31.01.2023 is under the process of implementation.

It was open for the present Review Petitioner as also the companion Review Petitioner (Mr. Bhosale & Mr.
Shambharkar) to come before us at that time and point out that there were error apparent on the face of record in our 1 st Order dated 31.01.2023.
Both the Review Petitioners have in fact chosen not to do so and have taken a chance to see how this Court reacts and has risked inviting our 2nd Order dated 27.02.2023.

5. On 27th February, 2023, we heard the said Contempt Petition as it was placed for reporting compliance, when the aforesaid two affidavits of Mr. Sambharkar and Sub-divisional Water Conservation Officer were on record.

At the cost of repetition, we must mention here that an impression was sought to be created in our mind that our 1st Order dated 31.01.2023 is under implementation and no so called error was pointed out to us.
With such situation at place, we heard the said Contempt Petition on 27.02.2023, when it was placed for reporting compliance.

6. From our 2nd Order dated 27th February, 2023, it is clear that learned AGP relied upon the said 2 affidavits and submitted that the payment of interest has been computed and the file is now sent to Divisional Commissioner, Pune and inability was expressed to Tikam page 9 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc make a statement as to when further implementation will take place.

In these set of facts,
we directed the Divisional Commissioner of Pune to sanction the amount of interest in a time bound manner and it was clarified that if the order is not complied with, appropriate further order will be passed under provisions of the Contempt of Courts Act.

7. From the aforesaid dissection of the facts, it is clear that we have passed the 2nd Order under Review, when no so called error apparent on the face of the record was pointed out to us though there was opportunity to do so.
We do not concede that there was error apparent on the face of the record in our 1 st Order under review, for reasons to follow.
But our 2 nd Order under review was passed on the impression being given to us that our 1 st Order is under implementation.

8. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, now let us consider the arguments advanced by learned senior counsel Mr. Kumbhakoni, who is appearing for present Review Petitioner as a matter of private engagement of legal services by the Review Petitioner through a private lawyer.
We hasten to add that the State Government has not filed any review.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Kumbhakoni argued that even if there is a mistake in the award, such mistake cannot be corrected by this Court in exercise of contempt jurisdiction.
He submitted that no interest is legally payable to the owners as rental compensation.
He submitted that in the contempt jurisdiction, this Court could not have ordered what is not ordered by the original order about which contempt is alleged.
Ms. Talekar, learned counsel for the original Petitioners, has vehemently opposed the review petition.
She submitted that original Order dated 28th January 2021 is admittedly not complied in as much as there is no decision on the Petitioners' claim of rental compensation.

She has also raised serious objection about locus of Petitioner, who is a government officer, who has passed the Award or who has filed affidavit in contempt petition, so far as companion review petitioner is concerned.
10. Let us consider the argument of legality first.

The judgment relied upon by Mr. Kumbhakoni to contend that 9% and 15% interest of rental compensation is not payable to the owners in the present case under law, is a judgment of full bench of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra v/s.
Kailash Shiva Rangari [2016(3) Mh. L.J 457].

entities.text:
State of Maharashtra v/s.
Kailash Shiva Rangari [2016(3) Mh. L.J 457]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Kumbhakoni urged that rental compensation in the form of 9% or 15% interest as opined by SDO, Mangalvedha in paragraph 3 (table) on page 4 of the said Award is Tikam page 11 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc legally not payable.
It appears that learned senior counsel has assumed that when we passed our 1st Order dated 31.01.2023, we were not aware of this full bench view.
But, that is not the case.

11. At the end of paragraph 31 of the said full bench Judgment, this Court has clearly stated that while deciding the said case, this Court was not concerned about rental compensation or damages, if possession of the land is de hors the provisions of the Act.

When we passed our 1 st Order on 31.01.2023, a copy of the Award was already shown to us in which, in paragraph 13 (about possession), it is clearly stated/admitted that the "system in action at the relevant time had illegally taken possession and completed work in 2008 itself and accordingly a certificate was issued to land owners that they are entitled to rental compensation"
12.

Being conscious of this fact that the possession of the property has been taken illegally from the owner (de hors the provisions of the law) on the day when we passed our 1 st Order on 31.01.2023,
we deemed it fit to insist on implementation of the original Order dated 28.01.2021 and sought implementation about the decision on the Petitioner's claim to rental compensation as provided in Award itself by complying with original Order dated 28.01.2021.

This was based on clear admission in the award that Tikam page 12 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc possession is taken illegally which is de hors the provisions of the Act as stated by the full bench read with a clear opinion expressed by SDO Mangalvedha that 9% and 15% interest is payable to the owner in para 3 (chart) on page 4 of the Award.

Udaysingh Bhosale vs Shridhar Shivaji Karande on 11 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158025006/
6 13.

entities.text: Udaysingh Bhosale vs Shridhar Shivaji Karande
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now lets go to the submission that the Court exercising contempt jurisdiction is not entitled to enter into question/s which have not been dealt with or decided in the judgment or order, violation of which is alleged.
Learned senior counsel Mr. Kumbhakoni relied upon the judgment of Hukum Chand Deswal v/s. Satish Raj Deswal (2020 SCC online SC 438) especially para 23 thereof.

entities.text: Hukum Chand Deswal v/s. Satish Raj Deswal (2020 SCC online SC 438)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no dispute about this proposition of law, as laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and we respectfully agree with it.
But, in the present case admittedly the original direction of this Court under Order dated 28.01.2021 to decide the claim of rental compensation is not obeyed.

It is material to note that we specifically asked Mr. Kumbhakoni to point out where in the Award passed by Review Petitioner Mr. Udaysingh Bhosale, the claim of rental compensation is decided (whether allowed or rejected was and is not our concern).
Mr. Kumbhakoni has fairly conceded that Review Petitioner Mr. Bhosale has not decided in the operative part of the Award anything about the rental compensation.

So, obviously we stand vouched in seeking implementation as directed under Tikam page 13 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc original Order about the rental compensation and therefore,
we have not entered any such question which is not decided in the original order, violation of which is alleged.

14. Lastly let us consider the submission of Mr. Kumbhakoni, wherein he tried to appeal to our judicial conscience by pointing out what is stated in paragraph just before para 28 of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Shri. Umed v/s. Raj Singh and Ors. (1975) 1 SCC 76 viz.
"to perpetuate an error is not heroism.

entities.text: Shri. Umed v/s. Raj Singh and Ors. (1975) 1 SCC 76
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To rectify it is the compulsion of judicial conscience.

In this we derive comfort and strength from the wise and inspiring words of Justice Bronson in Pierce Vs.
Delameter - a judge ought to be wise enough to know that he is fallible and therefore ever ready to learn; great and honest enough to discard all mere pride of opinion and follow truth wherever it may lead; and courageous enough to acknowledge his error".
We genuinely feel that such an appeal of high ground should have been reserved by Mr. Kumbhakoni for some other better case.

In the facts and circumstances of the present case, the Review Petitioner who had clear opportunity of coming before us and pointing out the so called error on the face of record (which we have already pointed out above as not existing), has chosen not to do so and has given us impression that our 1st Order dated 31.01.2023 was duly under Tikam page 14 of 16 RPNL 9220 of 2023.doc implementation,
thereby avoiding any contempt action against him.
15.
We must place on record that the State Government has chosen not to file any review in the matter.
But its officer, who is Review Petitioner is trying to seek review, alongwith other review Petitioner, for reasons best known to him.

We say so, because from two affidavits that were filed before us, we feel that two different offices of the Government are trying to avoid payment of compensation and are trying to push the liability on one-another.
It seems that different officers are taking different stand, which is nothing but shameful and unfortunate.
16. It is therefore clear that there is no error apparent on the face of record in both our orders dated 31.01.2023 and 27.02.2023.
No new material is shown to us, which the Review Petitioner could not show us when the orders were passed and no other sufficient reason exists.
In that view of the matter, no case for review is made out and the Review Petition is dismissed.
